evidence_tier: 3 (source review: class-test literals transcribed) for the three fixture scores, and 4 (independently derived) for every other asserted value, including all three self-similarity results, which are proved exact rather than compared to a tolerance. No tier 1 or tier 2 evidence: these five headers have no retained C++ output and no oracle driver was built for them.

class_test_review.independent_reimplementation: A throwaway numpy float32 model of binSpectrum_, SparseVector::dot and the agreeing-intensity expression reproduced all three class-test literals and quantified the f32-versus-f64 divergence used in the support documents (2.9e-8 relative for the contrast angle, 6.3e-9 to 2.8e-8 for the agreeing sum). It is a derivation aid, not committed code, and it raises these values no higher than evidence tier 4.

shared_peak_count_illegal_argument.operation: throw Exception::IllegalArgument on incompatible binning; message names 'bin size or spread' although isCompatible compares unit, size and offset

shared_peak_count_denominator.operation: size_t denominator = max(nonZeros(), nonZeros()); zero for two empty spectra, and the division at line 64 then yields NaN

shared_peak_count_intersection.operation: cwiseProduct of two sparse vectors; the result stores one coefficient per shared index without pruning zeros, so nonZeros() is the stored-index intersection size

contrast_angle_precondition.operation: OPENMS_PRECONDITION instead of a throw; a no-op in release builds, unlike both sibling functors

contrast_angle_float_dot.operation: const double sum1 = SparseVector<float>::dot(...); the reduction accumulates in float and is widened afterwards

contrast_angle_zero_guard.operation: if (sum1 * sum2 == 0.0) return 0.0; the source's own defined-zero guard against 0.0/0.0

contrast_angle_denominator_grouping.operation: numerator / sqrt(sum1 * sum2), not sqrt(sum1) * sqrt(sum2); the grouping is reproduced and makes self-similarity exactly 1.0

sum_agreeing_float_totals.operation: const double sum1 = SparseVector<float>::sum(); float accumulation widened to double

sum_agreeing_union_expression.operation: ((bins1 + bins2) * 0.5) - (bins1 - bins2).cwiseAbs(), then coeffs().cwiseMax(0).sum(); sparse addition spans the union and every operand stays float

sum_agreeing_unguarded_division.operation: min(sum_nn / ((sum1 + sum2) / 2.0), 1.0); the denominator is not checked for zero, and std::min(NaN, 1.0) returns NaN

functor_naming.operation: setName(<derived>) then defaultsToParam_() over an empty defaults tree; identical at BinnedSpectralContrastAngle.cpp:21 and BinnedSumAgreeingIntensities.cpp:21

native_boundaries: Incompatible binning is Error::InvalidValue from all three scorers, including BinnedSpectralContrastAngle whose source check is a release-build no-op

A zero denominator yields a defined score of 0 in BinnedSharedPeakCount and BinnedSumAgreeingIntensities, where the source divides by zero and returns NaN; BinnedSpectralContrastAngle already guards it upstream and the guard is kept verbatim
f32 overflow of a dot product or of an intensity sum is a checked error instead of an infinity carried into the score
sqrt is taken through a helper that refuses a negative or non-finite radicand
MAX_COMPARED_BINS = 4000000 combined stored bins is checked before any traversal; no scorer allocates, so a refusal leaves both inputs untouched

All reductions accumulate in f32 in ascending bin-index order, matching Eigen's scalar sparse walk; Eigen's dense redux may reassociate a large sum() under SIMD, so agreement there is to f32 reduction rounding rather than bit-exact
The protected precursor_mass_tolerance_ member of all three scorers is uninitialised, unwritten and unread upstream and has no counterpart

The pre-existing free functions binned_cosine, binned_shared_peak_count and binned_sum_agreeing_intensities are retained unchanged; they compute the same three scores in f64 with different degenerate-case and negative-bin policies and are not the header port
openmp: No #pragma omp in any of the five headers or their implementation files; no parallelism gap to record.
